Umar: After Muhammad's death in June 632, Umar pledged allegiance to Abu Bakr as the first caliph and served as his chief adviser.

Enron: United States. Enron Corporation was an American energy, commodities and services company based in Houston, Texas.

Otzma Yehudit: Israel. It is the ideological descendant of the outlawed Kach party.

In which country did the YSR Congress Party take place?
YSR Congress Party: India. The party was initially registered with Election Commission of India by Kolishetti Shiva Kumar.
Which of these was an official language of the Samanid Empire?
Samanid Empire: Persian. The Samanid Empire (Persian: سامانیان, romanized: Sāmāniyān) was a Persianate Sunni Muslim empire, ruled by a dynasty of Iranian dehqan origin, from 819 to 999.
Which of these is an official language of Order of Assassins?
Order of Assassins: Arabic. The two primary divisions were of the Persian Assassins in Alamut Castle and of the Levantine Assassins in Masyaf Castle.
Which of these was an official language of the Mughal Empire?
Mughal Empire: Persian. The Mughal Empire was an early modern empire in South Asia.
Who is credited with discovering La Tène culture?
La Tène culture: Bror Emil Hildebrand. The La Tène culture (French pronunciation: [la tɛn]) was a European Iron Age culture.
This former Minister of Water Resources succeeded Barham Salih as Iraq's head of state in 2022 — who is he?
Abdul Latif Rashid (born 10 August 1944), also known as Letif Reshid, is an Iraqi politician who served as the president of Iraq from 2022 to 2026.
This 6th-century king ended his people's wanderings by conquering northern Italy, beginning centuries of Lombard rule. Who was he?
Alboin (530s - 28 June 572) was king of the Lombards from about 560 until 572.

A War Democrat who ran on Lincoln's National Union ticket, he took the presidency after the assassination — then clashed so bitterly with Congress over Reconstruction that the House impeached him. Which 17th president was it?
Andrew Johnson (December 29, 1808 - July 31, 1875) was the 17th president of the United States, serving from 1865 to 1869.
A former communist who championed privatization, this president led a relatively less-authoritarian Central Asian state until the 2005 Tulip Revolution swept him out — who was he?
Askar Akayev (born 10 November 1944) is a Kyrgyz former politician who served as President of Kyrgyzstan from 1990 until being overthrown in the March 2005 Tulip Revolution.
George Washington trusted this major general enough to hand him command of West Point — which he then schemed to surrender to the British in 1780. Who was the would-be turncoat?
Benedict Arnold was British military officer (1741–1801).
Known as Perarignar Anna, this Dravidian-party leader and acclaimed Tamil writer led Madras State before dying just 20 days into leading its successor state — who is he?
C. N. Annadurai (15 September 1909 - 3 February 1969), also known as Perarignar Anna, was an Indian politician who was the founder and first general-secretary of the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK).
The longest-serving leader of Germany's Free Democratic Party, he served as federal finance minister from 2021 until his dismissal in 2024 sparked a government crisis — who is he?

Christian Lindner (born 7 January 1979) is a German retired politician of the Free Democratic Party (FDP) who was the Federal Minister of Finance from 2021 until his dismissal in 2024 during a government crisis.

The U.S. Navy's first-ever rear admiral, vice admiral, and admiral is remembered for a bold order at the Battle of Mobile Bay usually shortened to 'Damn the torpedoes ... full speed ahead.' Who was he?
Henri de La Tour d'Auvergne, Viscount of Turenne
David Farragut (also spelled Glascoe; July 5, 1801 - August 14, 1870) was a flag officer of the United States Navy during the American Civil War.
This New Zealand mountaineer, alongside Tenzing Norgay, became the first climber confirmed to reach the summit of Mount Everest, on 29 May 1953 — who is he?
Edmund Hillary (20 July 1919 - 11 January 2008) was a New Zealand mountaineer, explorer, and philanthropist.
According to Abrahamic tradition, this was the first woman created by God, whose name means 'living one' or 'source of life.' Who is she?
Eve is a figure from the Book of Genesis in the Old Testament.
This Congolese politician became his country's fifth president in 2019, succeeding his own late father as leader of the nation's oldest and largest political party. Who is he?
Félix Tshisekedi (born 13 June 1963) is a Congolese politician who is the fifth president of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, serving since 2019.
The youngest brother of Nicholas II, this Russian royal was briefly declared emperor after his sibling's 1917 abdication but declined to take power the very next day — who was he?
Grand Duke Michael Alexandrovich of Russia

This period of Japanese history corresponds to the reign of Emperor Akihito, beginning the day after the death of his father—posthumously renamed Emperor Shōwa—in January 1989, and ending with Akihito's 2019 abdication. What is this period called?
Heisei era was the period of Japanese history corresponding to the reign of Emperor Akihito from 8 January 1989 until his abdication on 30 April 2019.

A close ally of Deng Xiaoping who was purged twice by Mao during the Cultural Revolution, this Chinese leader headed the Communist Party from 1981 to 1987 — and his death in 1989 sparked national mourning. Who was he?
Hu Yaobang (20 November 1915 - 15 April 1989) was a Chinese politician who was a high-ranking official of the People's Republic of China.
Proclaimed emperor at just two months old, this Russian ruler was overthrown within a year and spent the rest of his life a prisoner before being killed — who was he?
Ivan VI of Russia was Emperor of Russia (1740–1741).
This California politician served two non-consecutive stints as governor decades apart, making him both the state's oldest and, at the time, its sixth-youngest governor — who is he?
Jerry Brown (born April 7, 1938) is an American lawyer, author, and politician who served as the 34th and 39th governor of California from 1975 to 1983 and 2011 to 2019.
Recognized by dozens of countries as Venezuela's legitimate president during the 2019 crisis, this opposition figure once co-founded the Popular Will party with Leopoldo López — who is he?
Juan Guaidó (born 28 July 1983) is a Venezuelan politician and opposition figure.

A medieval Iberian monarchy founded by the nobleman Pelagius, this was the first Christian political entity established after the Umayyad conquest in 711–720s, founded after his victory at the Battle of Covadonga in 722—what was this kingdom?

Kingdom of Asturias was a medieval monarchy in the Iberian Peninsula founded by the nobleman Pelagius. Under King Alfonso II (r. 791–842), the kingdom was firmly established with Alfonso's recognition as king of Asturias by Charlemagne and the Pope.
A former Brooklyn public defender and city council member, she became New York's 67th attorney general in 2019 and the first Black person to hold that post — who is she?
Letitia James (born October 18, 1958) is an American lawyer and politician from the state of New York.
His succession contested by his uncle Qavurt, this Seljuk sultan spent his reign battling the Karakhanids and bringing order to the Caucasus — who is he?
Malik-Shah I was the third sultan of the Seljuk Empire from 1072 to 1092, under whom the sultanate reached the zenith of its power and influence.
Founded around 320 BCE with its power base in Magadha, this Iron Age South Asian realm is chiefly documented through the later Edicts of a ruler named Ashoka — which empire?
Maurya Empire was a geographically extensive Iron Age historical power in South Asia with its power base in Magadha.

The son of a Michigan governor, he served a mission in France, earned joint Harvard degrees, then ran Bain & Company before becoming Massachusetts governor and a 2012 presidential nominee — who is he?

Mitt Romney (born March 12, 1947) is an American businessman and retired politician who served as a United States senator from Utah from 2019 to 2025 and as the 70th governor of Massachusetts from 2003 to 2007.
This Salvadoran leader ran an advertising company before entering politics, served as mayor of San Salvador, and founded the Nuevas Ideas party after being ousted from the FMLN — who is he?
Nayib Bukele (born 24 July 1981) is a Salvadoran politician and businessman who has served as the 43rd president of El Salvador since 2019.
Born in British Hong Kong, this Canadian politician became a Toronto school board trustee in 1985, later served as an NDP member of Parliament, and has been mayor of Toronto since 2023 — who is she?
Olivia Chow (born March 24, 1957) is a Canadian politician who has been the 66th and current mayor of Toronto since 2023.

This Roman emperor, the son of a freed slave, rose through a military career distinguishing himself in the Parthian War before briefly ruling for three months in 193 after Commodus's assassination — who was he?
Pertinax (1 August 126 - 28 March 193) was Roman emperor for the first three months of 193, succeeding Commodus and becoming the first ruler of the turbulent Year of the Five Emperors.

Officially known as the Religious Society of Friends, members of this Christian movement got their popular nickname after founder George Fox told a judge to 'quake before the authority of God' — what are they called?
Quakers are people who belong to the Religious Society of Friends, originally known as simply the Society of Friends, a historically Protestant Christian set of denominations.
A Czechoslovak-born media baron who escaped Nazi occupation and served as a British MP, he built Pergamon Press and later bought Mirror Group Newspapers and Macmillan — who was he?
Robert Maxwell (10 June 1923 - 5 November 1991) was a Czechoslovak-born British-French media proprietor and politician.
A former Arizona state legislator who was the first woman to lead a state senate, this moderate conservative became a famed swing vote — and the first woman on the U.S. Supreme Court. Who was she?

Sandra Day O'Connor (March 26, 1930 - December 1, 2023) was an American attorney, politician, and jurist who served as an associate justice of the Supreme Court of the United States from 1981 to 2006.

His campaigns against the Byzantines, Magyars, and Serbs stretched the First Bulgarian Empire to its greatest extent ever, ushering in a 'Golden Age' of culture — which ruler crowned from 893 to 927 is this?
Simeon I of Bulgaria (Church) was the ruler of the First Bulgarian Empire from 893 until his death in 927.
This former Singaporean cabinet minister also served as President of the National Olympic Council for nearly a decade before resigning all his posts in 2023 — who is he?
Tan Chuan-Jin (born 10 January 1969) is a Singaporean former politician and brigadier-general.
Leading a regional party he inherited, this politician was Maharashtra's chief minister from 2019 to 2022 and was ranked the most popular chief minister across 13 surveyed states — who is he?

Uddhav Thackeray (Marathi) is an Indian politician who served as the 19th Chief Minister of Maharashtra from 2019 to 2022 and the Leader of the House, Maharashtra Legislative Assembly from 2019 to 2022.
This German communist leader helped found the Weimar-era Communist Party of Germany and later served as East Germany's chief decision-maker and head of state until his death in 1973 — who was he?
Walter Ulbricht (30 June 1893 - 1 August 1973) was a German communist politician and revolutionary.
This Pakistani general served as his country's third president under martial law from 1969 to 1971, a presidency that oversaw the civil war leading to Bangladesh's secession — who was he?
Yahya Khan (4 February 1917 - 10 August 1980) was a Pakistani general who served as the third president of Pakistan from 1969 to 1971, under martial law.
A grandson of caliph Abu Bakr and the first child born to Islam's earliest converts, he led a rival caliphate based in Mecca during the Second Fitna until his death in 692 — who was he?
Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr: Arab leader of Mecca-based caliphate from 683 to 692.
Known as the 'Lion of Panjshir,' this Afghan commander led mujahideen forces against Soviet occupation before being assassinated in 2001 — who was he?
Ahmad Shah Massoud: Afghan military leader (1953–2001)

One of the original five Marshals of the Soviet Union, this ex-tsarist officer was rare enough that the Red Army actually trusted him — and he commanded its Southern Front against the Whites in the Civil War. Who was he?

He's the only Soviet politician who held power continuously from Lenin through Stalin and Khrushchev to retirement under Brezhnev — a longevity that spawned a Russian saying about lasting "from Ilyich to Ilyich." Who was this survivor?
Anastas Mikoyan: Soviet statesman and revolutionary (1895–1978)
Symbolized by seashells, myrtles, and doves, this Greek goddess of love and beauty was worshipped as a warrior at Sparta and syncretized with the Roman Venus. Who is she?
Aphrodite: Ancient Greek goddess of love. Aphrodite's major symbols include seashells, myrtles, roses, doves, sparrows, and swans.
The fifth IOC president and its only American leader, this fierce champion of amateurism is forever linked to the two Olympics he oversaw in Germany, in 1936 and 1972. Who was he?
Avery Brundage: President of the IOC from 1952 to 1972.
Known in Japan as the Nomonhan Incident, these decisive 1939 clashes saw Soviet general Georgy Zhukov combine tanks, aircraft, and infantry in tactics later reused at Stalingrad — what were they?
Battles of Khalkhin Gol: 1939 border clashes between Imperial Japan and the Soviet Union.
Before becoming Australia's 23rd prime minister, this Rhodes Scholar led the Australian Council of Trade Unions — who was he?
Bob Hawke: Prime Minister of Australia from 1983 to 1991.

Proclaimed in 220 AD by Cao Pi on foundations his father had laid, this was one of the major states of China's Three Kingdoms period — historians often prefix a family name to tell it apart from others. What is it?
Cao Wei: Chinese state (220–266) during the Three Kingdoms period.
Born into an Anglo-Irish Protestant landowning family, this Home Rule leader held the balance of power in the Commons before a long-running affair toppled him at just 45 — who was he?
Historians call his united realm of England, Denmark and Norway the 'North Sea Empire' — which Viking-age king, who won England's throne in 1016, earned the epithet 'the Great'?
Cnut: King of Denmark, Norway and England (c.995–1035)
His controversial 'junk food' defense at trial became notorious after he killed San Francisco's mayor and a fellow city supervisor in 1978 — who was he?
Dan White: American politician and assassin (1946–1985)
Married at St. Paul's Cathedral in July 1981, this royal became mother to two future princes and an international style icon — who was she?
Diana, Princess of Wales: Member of the British royal family (1961–1997)
This Torres Strait Islander's landmark High Court case overturned the doctrine of 'terra nullius' and led to the recognition of native title in Australia — who was he?
Eddie Mabo: Land rights activist for Indigenous Australians (1936–1992)

Born in Manchester's Moss Side, this British activist organized the suffragette movement that helped women win the vote in 1918 and was later named one of Time's 100 Most Important People of the 20th century — who is she?
The last monarch of a Middle Eastern kingdom, he took the throne at age three after his father died in a car crash, and was killed during the 1958 revolution that ended the monarchy — who was he?
Faisal II: King of Iraq from 1939 to 1958.
Founded by the Italian saint Francis of Assisi, this Catholic religious family includes the Order of Friars Minor for men and the Order of Saint Clare for nuns — what are its members called?
Franciscans: Group of religious orders within the Catholic Church connected with St. Francis of Assisi.

In January 2021, Reddit's r/wallstreetbets drove the stock of an American video game retailer up nearly 30-fold in a single month, inflicting massive losses on the hedge funds betting against it. What is this market event known as?
GameStop short squeeze: 2021 financial markets event.
The longest-serving Philippine president since Marcos, she first broke ground as the country's first female vice president before leading the nation from 2001 to 2010. Who is she?

Gloria Macapagal Arroyo: President of the Philippines from 2001 to 2010. Estrada was ousted by the Second EDSA Revolution in 2001, and Arroyo was sworn in as president by Chief Justice Hilario Davide Jr. on January 20.
Earning the title "Supreme Combatant" for ending France's 75-year protectorate, this Paris-trained lawyer became the first president of an independent North African nation in 1957 — who is he?
Habib Bourguiba: President of Tunisia from 1957 to 1987.
Often equated with the Israelites, this term for an ancient nomadic Semitic-speaking people appears 34 times across 32 verses of the Old Testament — what's the term?

A one-time WCW International World Heavyweight Champion, this Japanese wrestler-turned-politician later served as governor of Ishikawa Prefecture after a stint as education minister under Shinzo Abe — who is he?

Hiroshi Hase: Japanese politician and professional wrestler. As a professional wrestler, Hase primarily worked for New Japan Pro-Wrestling (NJPW), and also for All Japan Pro Wrestling (AJPW) and Stampede Wrestling.

Driven by WWI war debts and reparations demanded under the 1921 London Schedule of Payments, the German Papiermark lost nearly all its value between 1921 and 1923 — what is this economic crisis called?
Hyperinflation in the Weimar Republic: Period of extreme inflation in Germany during 1921–1923.
Co-owner of Macy's department store and briefly a U.S. congressman, this businessman died aboard the Titanic after his wife refused to leave the ship without him — who is he?
Isidor Straus: American politician, businessman, and Titanic sinking victim (1845–1912)
Hailed as the 'Father of the Constitution' for his role in drafting it and the Bill of Rights, this Virginia planter went on to serve as the fourth U.S. president — who is it?
James Madison: Founding Father, U.S. president from 1809 to 1817.

This aviation pioneer earned the Medal of Honor for a famous bombing raid on Japan during World War II, and was also credited as the first pilot to complete a flight using instruments alone — who is he?
Jimmy Doolittle: American general and aviator (1896–1993)

A former police officer turned serial killer, this Californian terrorized the state from 1974 to 1986 under a chilling roster of nicknames — the East Area Rapist, the Original Night Stalker, the Visalia Ransacker. Who is he?
Joseph James DeAngelo: American serial rapist and serial killer (born 1945)
Known as the "Merrie Monarch" for his singing and ukulele playing, this last king of Hawaiʻi lifted the public ban on hula — who was he?
Kalākaua: King of Hawaii from 1874 to 1891.

Surviving five assassination attempts and years of imprisonment and exile for his democratization activism, this opposition leader finally won election as South Korea's eighth president in 1997 — who is he?
Kim Dae-jung: President of South Korea from 1998 to 2003.
In Arthurian legend, this enchantress figure gifts Excalibur to the king, raises the knight Lancelot, and later helps carry the dying king to Avalon — who or what is she?
Lady of the Lake: Sorceress in Arthurian legend. As either single character or multiple ones, the figure of the Lady of the Lake often appears in various roles in the works of modern culture.

This anti-authoritarian political current rejects both state ownership and private property, uniting strands of anarchism that reached its height during the 1936 Spanish Revolution — what is it called?
Libertarian socialism: Political philosophy. Libertarian socialism is an anti-authoritarian and anti-capitalist political current that emphasises self-governance and workers' self-management.
A wealthy merchant who bribed his way into making a hostage prince the heir to the Qin throne, this chancellor later served as regent for the boy who became China's First Emperor — who is he?
Lü Buwei: Chinese merchant and politician of the Qin state (291–235 BCE)
Heir to a former Maharaja and founder of the Lakshya Trust charity, he is widely considered the first openly gay prince in the world — who is he?
Manvendra Singh Gohil: Hereditary Prince of Rajpipla.
Born in August 1975, this independent lawmaker sat in Japan's House of Representatives — who is he?
Founder of the agrarian movement AGROunia, this politician served as Poland's deputy minister of agriculture from 2023 to 2025 — who is he?
Michał Kołodziejczak: Polish politician. Michał Kołodziejczak (born 14 September 1988) is a Polish politician and founder of AGROunia.
This former Afghan president took shelter in a UN compound in Kabul after a failed flight to India, living there until the Taliban's 1996 capture of the city ended in his assassination — who was he?
Mohammad Najibullah: Leader of Afghanistan from 1987 to 1992.
Serving as Israel's prime minister from 2021 to 2022, this politician and former special-forces soldier co-founded the tech company Cyota after growing up in Haifa — who is he?
Naftali Bennett: Prime Minister of Israel from 2021 to 2022. Bennett has served as the head of Bennett 2026 since 2025; the party is allied with Yesh Atid as part of an alliance called Together.
A loyal Stalinist who rose through the Soviet hierarchy during the purges, this politician served as Premier of the Soviet Union from 1955 to 1958 — who is he?
A brigadier general who seized power in a 1989 coup and ruled Sudan under various titles until a 2019 coup toppled him, after which he was jailed and convicted of corruption — who is he?
Omar al-Bashir: President of Sudan from 1989 to 2019.
He left school at 14 yet became Australia's 24th prime minister, having first served as treasurer under Bob Hawke before taking the top job in 1991 — who is he?
Paul Keating: Prime Minister of Australia from 1991 to 1996.
Educated in New Zealand and the United States, this Thai businessman led the Move Forward Party, successor to the dissolved Future Forward Party — who is he?
Pita Limjaroenrat: Thai businessman and politician (born 1980)

Fought almost entirely at sea from 1798 to 1800 after France began seizing American ships, this undeclared conflict pitted the young United States against the French First Republic — what was it called?
Quasi-War: Undeclared naval war between the United States and France, 1798–1800.

Hitler called him 'the man with the iron heart' — this chief of the Reich Security Main Office and principal architect of the Holocaust was also Deputy Reich-Protector of Bohemia and Moravia. Who was he?
Reinhard Heydrich: German high-ranking Nazi official (1904–1942)

A Russian oligarch who once governed the remote Chukotka region and grew rich through Yeltsin's loans-for-shares scheme, he became famous in England as the former owner of Chelsea Football Club. Who is he?
In Buddhism it caps the Noble Eightfold Path, and in the Yoga Sutras of Patanjali it's the eighth and final limb of Ashtanga Yoga — what meditative state is this?
Samadhi: State of meditative consciousness. Samādhi (Pali and Sanskrit: समाधि), in the Indian religions, is a state of meditative consciousness.
Once a commander of Alexander the Great's elite infantry, this Macedonian general later ruled Asia Minor, Syria, Mesopotamia, and Iran, founding an empire that bore his name — who was he?
Seleucus I Nicator: Macedonian general, Diadochus, and founder of the Seleucid Empire.
Spanning Emperor Hirohito's reign from 1926 to 1989, this period saw Japan's wartime totalitarian turn, defeat in World War II, and a nearly seven-year American-led occupation — which era?
Shōwa era: Period of Japanese history (1926–1989)

Traditionally blamed on Queen Catherine de' Medici, this 1572 wave of Catholic mob violence targeted Huguenots gathered in Paris for a royal wedding during the French Wars of Religion. By what name is it known?
St. Bartholomew's Day massacre: 1572 killing of Huguenots in France.
Nicknamed for both his towering height and his 23-year run, this architect of the 'Swedish Model' welfare state holds the record as his country's longest-serving prime minister — who was he?
Tage Erlander: Prime Minister of Sweden from 1946 to 1969.
Of African descent through his mother, this French Revolutionary Wars general was one of only a handful of men of color to command European troops as a general officer in that era — who is he?
An economist who entered parliament via a 1981 by-election, this Samoan politician went on to serve as his country's prime minister from 1998 all the way to 2021 — who is he?
Tuilaʻepa Saʻilele Malielegaoi: Prime Minister of Samoa from 1998 to 2021. After Tofilau resigned in 1998, Tuilaʻepa became the prime minister and HRPP party leader.

Set to become just the fourth queen to rule her Scandinavian kingdom in her own right — and the first since 1720 — she is heir apparent thanks to a 1980 law that was Western Europe's first with absolute primogeniture. Who is she?
Victoria, Crown Princess of Sweden: Heir apparent to the Swedish throne (born 1977)
Erupting in 1793 as a peasant revolt that turned Royalist, this French Revolutionary-era conflict was fought south of the Loire river and gave its combatants the nickname "Vendeans" — what was it?
War in the Vendée: 1793–1796 set of battles between the French revolutionaries and the royalists.

Known as the 'Mother of the Nation,' this South African anti-apartheid activist and politician served in parliament and led the ANC Women's League after marrying the country's future president in 1958 — who is she?
Winnie Mandela: South African activist and politician (1936–2018)
This Central European nation emerged after World War I as a union of South Slavic peoples, survived until 1992, and was born from the merger of Serbia with a provisional state. What country was this?
Who among these was born first?
Eratosthenes (born 276 BC) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these people was born first?
William Osler (born 1849) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four was founded earliest?

Fortran (founded 1957) is the earliest of the four. Fortran (formerly FORTRAN) is a third-generation, compiled, imperative programming language designed for numeric computation and scientific computing.
Which of these four dates back furthest?
MUMPS (founded 1966) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is a physicist?
Ernest Lawrence is a physicist. A graduate of the University of South Dakota and University of Minnesota, Lawrence obtained a PhD in physics at Yale in 1925.
Who among these is a chemist?
Glenn T. Seaborg is a chemist. Throughout his career, Seaborg worked for arms control.
What is the atomic number of Boron?
Boron is a chemical element; it has symbol B and atomic number 5.
In what year was Elon Musk born?
Elon Musk: Elon Reeve Musk (EE-lon; born June 28, 1971) is a businessman and former public official who is the CEO and largest shareholder of Tesla and SpaceX.
In what year was Radium discovered?
Radium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ra and atomic number 88.
In what year was Copper discovered?
Copper is a chemical element; it has symbol Cu (from Latin cuprum) and atomic number 29.
Mil Mi-17: Kazan Helicopters. It is known as the Mi-8M series in Russian service.
Which country is Curtiss P-40 Warhawk from?
Curtiss P-40 Warhawk: United States. The Curtiss P-40 Warhawk is an American single-engined, single-seat, all-metal fighter-bomber that first flew in 1938.
Who is credited with discovering Ruthenium?
Ruthenium: Karl Ernst Claus. Ruthenium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ru and atomic number 44.
Who is credited with discovering Aniline?
Aniline: Otto Unverdorben. Aniline (From Portuguese: anil, meaning 'indigo shrub', and -ine indicating a derived substance) is an organic compound with the formula C6H5NH2.
Who is credited with discovering Lie group?
Lie group: Sophus Lie. Combining these two ideas, one obtains a continuous group where multiplying points and their inverses is continuous.
With the formula (CH3)2CO, this volatile solvent is produced by the millions of tonnes yearly, much of it to make precursors for plastics like bisphenol A — what is it?
Acetone (2-propanone or dimethyl ketone) is an organic compound with the formula (CH3)2CO.
This genus of more than 650 flowering succulent species includes a 'true' member cultivated worldwide as the standard source for a soothing pharmaceutical gel — what's the genus?
Aloe (also written Alo) is a genus containing over 650 species of flowering succulent plants.

Named in 1835 from the Greek for 'flower' and 'dark blue,' these pH-shifting pigments paint blueberries, black rice, and some autumn leaves anything from red to purple to nearly black — what are they?

Anthocyanin (from Ancient Greek (nthos) 'flower' and / (kuneos/kuanos) 'dark blue'), also called anthocyans, are water-soluble vacuolar pigments that, depending on their pH, may appear red, pink, purple, blue, or black.

Named for the Ancient Greek word for 'star' after its flower shape, this group of roughly 170 mostly Eurasian perennial plants is also known for its late-blooming 'Michaelmas daisies' — which plant group?
Aster (genus) is a genus of perennial flowering plants in the family Asteraceae.
A civil-engineering graduate who first reshaped his father's firm toward real estate, this Frenchman now chairs the world's largest luxury goods company — who is he?
Bernard Arnault (born 5 March 1949) is a French businessman.
This branch of biology studies how plants have grown, reproduced, and evolved over the last 3.5 billion years of life on Earth — what field is it?
Botany is the branch of natural science and biology that studies the growth, reproduction and evolution of plants over the last 3.5 billion years of life on earth.

The largest land bird in North America went fully extinct in the wild in 1987 when every survivor was captured for breeding — which critically endangered vulture has since returned to the Grand Canyon and beyond?
California condor (Gymnogyps californianus) is a New World vulture and the largest North American land bird.
This worldwide family of over 5,000 fly species — found everywhere except the Antarctic and Arctic — includes the biting midges also known as sand flies — what is it called?
Ceratopogonidae is a family of flies colloquially known as no-see-ums, sand flies, or biting midges, generally 1-3 millimetres (116-18 in) in length.
An American naturalist who surveyed wildlife in Labrador, he turned what he learned there into quick-freezing methods that launched the modern frozen-food industry. Who was he?
Clarence Birdseye (December 9, 1886 - October 7, 1956) was an American inventor, entrepreneur, and naturalist, who is widely considered the founder of the modern frozen food industry.
Thanks to variations in the OR6A2 gene, some people taste this Mediterranean herb as fresh and citrusy while others swear it tastes like soap — its leaves are called cilantro in the US. What is it?
Coriander is an annual herb in the family Apiaceae.
What unit of time, roughly 24 hours long, marks one full rotation of the Earth relative to the Sun and drives the circadian rhythms of most living things?
Day is the time period of a full rotation of the Earth with respect to the Sun.
Fossils of this Late Devonian armored fish genus, among the earliest vertebrate apex predators ever, have turned up from Morocco to Poland to North America — which genus?
Dunkleosteus is an extinct genus of large arthrodire ("jointed-neck") fish that existed during the Late Devonian period, about 382-358 million years ago.
Practitioners of this zoological discipline have identified more than 1.3 million species within a single group of arthropods — what is it called?
Entomology (ntomon), meaning "insect", and (lgos), meaning "study", is the branch of zoology that focuses on insects.
Native to Mediterranean shores, this hardy perennial herb tastes much like anise and lends its flavor to absinthe; one variety swells into a bulb you can eat as a vegetable — what is it?
Fennel (Foeniculum vulgare) is a flowering plant species in the carrot family.
This Canadian physician and author has written five books exploring how childhood trauma shapes conditions from ADHD to addiction, arguing recovery must address underlying emotional pain — who is he?
Gabor Maté (born January 1944) is a Canadian physician and author.

Found in northern South America, this tarantula is the world's heaviest and longest-bodied spider, tipping the scales at over 170 grams, though a huntsman spider still beats it on leg span — what spider is it?
Goliath birdeater (Theraphosa blondi) is a large spider that belongs to the tarantula family Theraphosidae.
Tapeworms, flukes, and roundworms burrowing into the gut and beyond all fall under this macroparasitic disease — a neglected tropical illness better known as worm infection. What is it?
Helminthiasis is any macroparasitic disease of humans and other animals in which a part of the body is infected with parasitic worms, known as helminths.
Dissolved in water it yields a notoriously corrosive acid, yet it's also the main industrial route to fluorine and a feedstock for Teflon-style polymers like PTFE — which colorless compound is it?
Hydrogen fluoride is an inorganic compound with chemical formula HF.

Acting as the eye's diaphragm in optical terms, this thin ring-shaped structure controls how much light reaches the retina by adjusting the pupil's size, and also determines a person's eye color — name this structure?

Iris (anatomy) (pl.: irides or irises) is a thin, ring-shaped structure in the eye in most mammals and birds that is responsible for controlling the diameter and size of the pupil, and thus the amount of light reaching the retina.
This Liverpool-born mathematician roamed from finite groups to knot theory, but is best loved for inventing a famous cellular automaton called the Game of Life — who was he?
John Horton Conway (26 December 1937 - 11 April 2020) was an English mathematician.
Named from the Greek word for 'the hidden one', this colorless, odorless noble gas with atomic number 36 is used in fluorescent lamps and high-powered gas lasers. Name the element?
Krypton (from Ancient) is a chemical element; it has symbol Kr and atomic number 36.

First isolated from linseed oil and named from the Latin words for 'flax' and 'oil,' this omega-6 polyunsaturated fatty acid is one of the two essential fats humans must get from their diet — which acid?
Linoleic acid (LA) is an organic compound with the formula CH3(CH2)4CH=CHCH2CH=CH(CH2)7COOH.

A chemical element with symbol Mg and atomic number 12, it's a shiny gray metal with low density and high chemical reactivity that readily reacts with air to form a thin passivation oxide coating. What element is this?
Magnesium is a chemical element; it has symbol Mg and atomic number 12. The free metal burns with a brilliant-white light.
First isolated from a cow's pineal gland in 1958 because it could lighten the skin of frogs, this nighttime hormone went on to become famous for governing the sleep-wake cycle — what is it?
Melatonin is a natural compound produced by various organisms, including bacteria and eukaryotes.
This SI base unit for amount of substance, symbol mol, is defined so that one unit contains exactly 6.02214076×10²³ elementary entities — what is it called?
Mole (unit) (symbol mol) is a unit of measurement, the base unit in the International System of Units (SI) for amount of substance.

Which form of alternative medicine, rooted in vitalism and folk healing rather than evidence, gathers 'natural' and 'self-healing' practices ranging from discredited homeopathy to accepted psychotherapy?
Naturopathy is a form of alternative medicine. The ethics of naturopathy have been called into question by medical professionals and its practice has been characterized as quackery.
Despite counting the killer whale and pilot whale among its roughly forty species, this marine mammal family is more closely related to porpoises than to true whales — what family is it?
Oceanic dolphin are a widely distributed family of dolphins that live in the sea.
Located above, below, between, and behind the eyes, these four paired air-filled cavities take their names from the skull bones that contain them — what are they?
Paranasal sinuses are a group of four paired air-filled spaces that surround the nasal cavity.

This insect order's scientific name derives from the Ancient Greek word for 'apparition' or 'phantom' — fitting for a group whose members are famous for disguising themselves as twigs and leaves. What order is this?
Phasmatodea (also known as Phasmida or Phasmatoptera) are an order of insects whose members are variously known as stick insects, stick bugs, walkingsticks, stick animals, or bug sticks.

This large, nearly ubiquitous family of flowering plants provides the world's cereal crops, bamboo, and the plants used in lawns and pastures, ranking as the fifth-largest plant family with roughly 12,000 species — what family is this?
Poaceae (poh-(y)e), also called Gramineae (gr-(y)e), is a large and nearly ubiquitous family of monocotyledonous flowering plants commonly known as true grasses.

This sympathomimetic medication is best known as a nasal decongestant, though at higher doses it can act as a stimulant and appetite suppressant, making it a common drug of abuse — what's the compound called?
Pseudoephedrine is a sympathomimetic medication which is used as a nasal decongestant to treat nasal congestion.
Named from the Latin word for 'net', this light-sensitive layer lining the back of the eye functions much like the film or sensor inside a camera. Name this part of the eye?

This zodiac constellation, whose Latin name means 'archer,' is traditionally depicted as a centaur drawing a bow, and its territory in the southern sky contains the center of the Milky Way galaxy. What constellation is this?
Sagittarius (constellation) is one of the constellations of the zodiac and is located in the Southern celestial hemisphere.

Triggered by certain serotonergic medications, this group of symptoms can range from mild high blood pressure to severe, potentially fatal spikes in body temperature and dangerous muscle breakdown — what's it called?
Serotonin syndrome (SS) consists of a group of symptoms that may occur with the use of certain serotonergic medications or drugs.

This genus of about 60 evergreen flowering plant species, native to the tropical Americas and Southeast Asia, is commonly grown as a houseplant valued for its large leaves and elegant white blooms — what genus is it?
Spathiphyllum is a genus of about 60 species of monocotyledonous flowering plants in the family Araceae, native to tropical regions of the Americas and southeastern Asia.
Educated in Rotterdam through World War II, this Indonesian economist later served as minister of finance, trade, and research under two different presidents — who was he?
Sumitro Djojohadikusumo (27 May 1917 - 9 March 2001) was an Indonesian statesman and one of the country's most influential economists.
Used to treat asthma and COPD, this methylxanthine drug — a cousin of caffeine — turns up in trace amounts in tea, chocolate, and yerba mate. What is it?
Theophylline is a drug that inhibits phosphodiesterase and blocks adenosine receptors.
Formed from glycerol bonded to three fatty acids, these molecules make up the main constituents of body fat in humans and are also major components of human skin oil — what are they?
Triglyceride (from tri- and glyceride; also TG, triacylglycerol, TAG, or triacylglyceride) is an ester derived from glycerol and three fatty acids.
This chronic autoimmune disorder strips patches of skin of their pigment, and in antiquity was often wrongly conflated with leprosy — what is it?
Vitiligo is a chronic autoimmune disorder that causes patches of skin to lose pigment or color; these vary in size and can appear anywhere on the body.
Almost always found combined with lanthanide minerals and never on its own in nature, this element with symbol Y is a key ingredient in the phosphors used inside LEDs — which element?
Yttrium is a chemical element; it has symbol Y and atomic number 39.

The only legitimate child of the poet Lord Byron, this English mathematician saw that Charles Babbage's analytical engine could do far more than crunch numbers — earning her a reputation as the first computer programmer. Who was she?
Shining as the brightest star in Taurus some 67 light-years from Earth, this red giant has swollen to roughly 45 times the Sun's size despite a cooler surface — which star?
Aldebaran: Taurus Brightest Star. Aldebaran (Arabic: الدَّبَرَان, lit. 'The Follower') is a star in the zodiac constellation of Taurus.
Used to treat dangerous heart rhythms like ventricular fibrillation, which drug can take weeks to work when swallowed but carries risks of lung, liver, thyroid, and eye toxicity?
Awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2008 for his AIDS-relief work on PEPFAR, this immunologist directed the U.S. allergy and infectious-disease institute from 1984 to 2022. Who is he?
Known as common wormwood, this bitter herb native to North Africa and temperate Eurasia lends its name and flavor to a notorious green spirit — which plant?
Artemisia absinthium: Species of plant. It is grown as an ornamental plant and is used as an ingredient in the spirit absinthe and some other alcoholic beverages.
Whose name derives from the Sanskrit word 'nimba,' this Mahogany-family tree native to South Asia is the source of a widely used pesticidal oil — which species, and not one of these animals?
Azadirachta indica: Species of plant. Azadirachta indica, commonly known as neem, margosa, nimtree or Indian lilac, is a tree in the Mahogany family Meliaceae.
Named after a barberry-related plant genus and glowing bright yellow under ultraviolet light, this alkaloid was recorded in an ancient Chinese herbal medicine text around 200 BC. What compound is it?
Native to tropical South America, this large non-venomous member of family Boidae is a fixture of private collections thanks to its wildly variable color patterns — what species is it?
Known for a widely viewed 2010 TEDx talk on shame and vulnerability, which academic wrote six consecutive number-one New York Times bestsellers, including Daring Greatly?
Brené Brown: American academic, speaker and author.
This highly soluble white crystalline salt is spread on icy roads for de-icing and, in its anhydrous form, works as a moisture-absorbing desiccant. What compound is it?
Calcium chloride: Chemical compound. The compound is a white crystalline solid at room temperature, and it is highly soluble in water.
Native to the Mediterranean, this legume tree's seed pods are ground into a chocolate substitute, while its seeds yield a common food thickener known as locust bean gum — which tree?
Carob: Small tree grown for its edible pods and landscaping.
This goat-antelope roams mountain ranges from the Pyrenees to the Caucasus and has even been introduced to New Zealand's South Island — which animal?
Named after a 17th-century English physician, this ring-shaped network of arteries supplies blood to the brain in humans and other vertebrates — what is it called?
Circle of Willis: Circulatory anastomosis that supplies blood to the brain and surrounding structures.
In this prolonged state of deep unconsciousness, a person cannot be awakened, shows no normal sleep-wake cycle, and may even be induced deliberately during general anesthesia — what is it?
Coma: State of unconsciousness. The person may experience respiratory and circulatory problems due to the body's inability to maintain normal bodily functions.
Going by puma, mountain lion, catamount, and panther depending on where you stand, this big cat is the most widely distributed wild land mammal in the Americas — what is it?
Cougar: Wild cat species native to the Americas.
Native to Mexico and Central America, this tuberous flowering plant blooms in nearly every hue except blue, and its tubers store energy as inulin rather than starch — what is it?
Dahlia: Genus of flowering plants in the daisy family Asteraceae.

Historically defined by having two embryonic seed leaves, this once-standard division of flowering plants covers around 200,000 species but turned out not to share one common ancestor — which plant group?
Dicotyledon: Historical grouping of flowering plants.
One of the very first vertebrate apex predators on Earth, this armor-plated, jointed-neck fish patrolled open Devonian seas some 380 million years ago — which genus?
This Russian economist served as Vladimir Putin's economic adviser before becoming governor of the Central Bank of Russia — who is she?

Elvira Nabiullina: Russian economist and Governor of the Bank of Russia. Elvira Sakhipzadovna Nabiullina (born 29 October 1963) is a Russian economist and current governor of the Central Bank of Russia.
This branch of anthropology studies individual cultures through participant observation, with roots in early 20th-century social science — what is this field called?
Ethnography: Systematic study of people and cultures.
First described from a skull in 1846 and initially mistaken for a porpoise, this highly social oceanic dolphin gets its common name from a skull resembling that of the orca — which species?
False killer whale: Species of oceanic dolphin in the genus Pseudorca.
Discovered in Dubna in 1999, this superheavy synthetic element (number 114) honors a Russian physicist whose name in Cyrillic explains why its spelling swaps a 'yo' for an 'e' — which element?
Flerovium: Chemical element with atomic number 114 (Fl)

Nicknamed for their nighttime cries, these small nocturnal African primates are, according to the African Wildlife Foundation, the continent's most successful strepsirrhine group — what are they commonly called?
Galago: Family of primates. The Ghanaian name aposor is given to them because of their firm grip on branches.
Found in the Eastern Atlantic and the Mediterranean, this prized food fish from the porgy family is a cornerstone of European aquaculture — which fish?
Gilt-head bream: Mediterranean fish. It is a highly esteemed food fish and an important species in aquaculture.
Standing up to a meter tall with a white head marked by a black stripe to its crest, this wading bird of Europe, Asia, and Africa hunts motionless beside water — what is it?
Grey heron: Long-legged predatory wading bird.
Powered by a Rolls-Royce Avon turbojet and featuring swept wings, this 1950s RAF fighter set a world air speed record of over 727 mph in September 1953 — which aircraft?
Hawker Hunter: 1950s family of British fighter aircraft.
Overharvested in the 19th century for old-fashioned bloodletting, this European leech remains endangered in many countries today — which species?
Hirudo medicinalis: Species of annelid worm.
Teaching philosophy and astronomy in Roman-era Alexandria, this Neoplatonist is considered the first female mathematician whose life is well documented — who is she?
Sitting on the electromagnetic spectrum between visible light and microwaves, this invisible radiation makes up most of the black-body glow given off by objects near room temperature — what is it?

Infrared: Form of electromagnetic radiation. Infrared (IR; sometimes called infrared light) is electromagnetic radiation (EMR) with wavelengths longer than that of visible light but shorter than microwaves.
Working under Tamerlane around 1400, this Persian astronomer and mathematician produced work that mostly never reached Europe and stays largely unpublished — who is it?
Jamshid al-Kashi: Persian astronomer and mathematician (c. 1380–1429)
Before flying on Space Shuttle mission STS-128 in 2009, this Mexican-American engineer helped develop digital mammography equipment at Lawrence Livermore — who is he?
José M. Hernández: American engineer, vintner, and former NASA astronaut.
Bred for their dazzling colors since the early 19th century in Niigata, Japan, these ornamental carp come in patterns like Kōhaku and Shōwa Sanshoku — what are they?
Koi: Colored varieties of Amur carp.

Native to the dry grasslands and deserts of Afghanistan, Iran, Pakistan, India, and Nepal, this ground-dwelling reptile is so widely captive-bred it's considered the first domesticated species of its kind — what is it?
Leopard gecko: Species of reptile. The leopard gecko is a popular pet, and due to extensive captive breeding it is sometimes referred to as the first domesticated species of lizard.

This American stealth strike fighter comes in three flavors — conventional, short-takeoff/vertical-landing, and carrier-based — and with 883 in service is the world's fourth-most-numerous military aircraft. What is it?

Lockheed Martin F-35 Lightning II: American stealth multirole fighter aircraft. The Lockheed Martin F-35 Lightning II is an American family of single-seat, single-engine, supersonic stealth strike fighters.
With the formula MgCl2, this colorless salt forms hydrates and serves as the principal precursor to large-scale production of its namesake metal — what is it?
Magnesium chloride: Inorganic salt: MgCl2 and its hydrates. It forms hydrates MgCl2·nH2O, where n can range from 1 to 12.
Widely brewed as a calming herbal tea despite limited clinical evidence for its effects, this annual plant in the daisy family goes by the nickname 'scented mayweed' — which plant?
Matricaria chamomilla: Species of flowering plant.
Once made by roasting wood — hence its old name 'wood alcohol' — this simplest alcohol smells much like the drinkable kind but is far more poisonous. What is it?

A hemiparasitic plant that taps into its host tree via a structure called the haustorium to steal water and nutrients, its European species was introduced to Northern California in 1900 — what plant is it?
Mistletoe: Common name for various parasitic plants.
Its Inuktitut name means 'the bearded one,' and males emit a strong odor during rut to attract mates — which thick-coated Arctic mammal is this?
Muskox: Species of arctic land mammal.
Popularized by neurologist George Beard in the 1860s, this diagnosis described fatigue, anxiety, and heart palpitations often blamed on the stresses of modern life — what was the condition called?
Grown worldwide as ornamentals in ponds and known to gardeners simply as water lilies, this widespread genus of aquatic plants also includes species considered weeds — which genus?
Nymphaea: Genus of aquatic plants. Nymphaea is a genus of hardy and tender aquatic plants in the family Nymphaeaceae.
This Romanian-American engineer served as Team Principal of the Alpine Formula One team from February 2022 to July 2023 — who is he?
Otmar Szafnauer: American-Romanian engineer, F1 team lead.
Found in mice, cats, birds, humans, and dogs but absent in whales and most reptiles, this triangular bone is the body's largest sesamoid — what is it?
Patella: Kneecap, bone covering knee joint.
Named from the Greek word for 'apparition' due to their leaf-like camouflage, this insect order includes stick insects and leaf insects. What's it called?
Phasmatodea: Order of stick and leaf insects.
Members of this eukaryotic kingdom mostly make their own food with chlorophyll, though parasitic kinds have ditched photosynthesis entirely to feed off others — what kingdom is it?
Plant: Kingdom of organisms. Historically, as in Aristotle's biology, the plant kingdom encompassed all living things that were not animals, and included algae and fungi.
This corticosteroid treats conditions from rheumatoid arthritis to asthma but can cause bone loss and psychiatric side effects with long-term use — what is it called?
Prednisolone: Corticosteroid medication. It can be taken by mouth, injected into a vein, used topically as a skin cream, or as eye drops.
Often starting as a blood clot in the leg that travels to the lungs, this blockage can cause chest pain on breathing in, coughing up blood, and sudden death — what is the condition?

Pulmonary embolism: Blockage of an artery in the lungs. Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a blockage of an artery in the lungs by a substance that has moved from elsewhere in the body through the bloodstream (embolism).

Native to the eastern Himalayas and southwestern China, this small mammal sports dense reddish-brown fur, a ringed tail, and curved semi-retractile claws for climbing — and was the original bearer of its famous name. What is it?
Red panda: Species of mammal in Asia.
First created in 1994 near Darmstadt, Germany, this extremely radioactive synthetic element is named for the physicist who discovered X-rays — which element is it?
Roentgenium: Chemical element with atomic number 111 (Rg)
Also called elder or elderberry, this tree or shrub's flowers and berries are traditionally used to make cordial and wine — what's its scientific name?
Sambucus nigra: Species of flowering plant in the moschatel family.
The sole living species in its genus, this coastal California evergreen is the tallest tree species on Earth, reaching over 116 meters and living 2,200 years or more. What is it?
Sequoia sempervirens: Species of tree. Sequoia sempervirens is the sole living species of the genus Sequoia in the cypress family Cupressaceae (formerly treated in Taxodiaceae).

Its last natural case appeared in 1977, and in 1980 the WHO declared it the only human disease ever wiped off the Earth — which scourge, known for fluid-filled blisters that scarred survivors, was it?
It's the largest order of reptiles — lizards and snakes alike — set apart by horny scales they periodically shed and a hinged upper jaw that lets snakes gape around big prey. Which order?
Squamata: Order of reptiles. The now-extinct mosasaurs reached lengths over 14 m (46 ft).
Starting his career as a materials engineer and later overseeing the launch of Chrome and Google Drive, who has served as CEO of both Google and its parent company since 2015 and 2019 respectively?
Sundar Pichai: CEO of Alphabet Inc. and Google (born 1972)
Feigning injury or authority to lure victims to his car, this American serial killer murdered young women across five states in the mid-1970s before revisiting their graves. Who was he?
Known commonly as garden thyme or German thyme, this flowering plant belongs to the mint family — which species is it?
Thymus vulgaris: Species of flowering plant.
This condition involves a long-term urge to pull out one's own hair, most often from the scalp or around the eyes, and is more common among those with OCD — what is it?
Formed by the fusion of membrane vesicles, this shapeless organelle in plant and fungal cells is basically a water-filled storage sac that can even hold engulfed solids. What is it?
Vacuole: Membrane-bound organelle in cells containing fluid.
Descended from a wild bovine ancestor, this large domesticated animal from the Indian subcontinent now also grazes fields in Italy, the Balkans, and Australia — what is it?
Water buffalo: Species of large bovine. The wild water buffalo (Bubalus arnee) is most probably the ancestor of the domestic water buffalo.
Making up only about 1% of described fungal species, this single-celled organism reproduces by budding or fission and is so tiny it usually measures just 3 to 4 micrometres across — what is it?
The symbol for argon is Ar. Argon is a chemical element; it has symbol Ar and atomic number 18.
What is the chemical symbol for cadmium?
The symbol for cadmium is Cd. Cadmium is a chemical element; it has symbol Cd and atomic number 48.

Prince Edward, Duke of Edinburgh (Edward Antony Richard Louis; born 10 March 1964), is a member of the British royal family.
